Nucleus.title: Nucleus
Nucleus.description: Represents a core entity or project within BindNexus, to which bind codes can be associated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Nucleus entity.

description.description: A concise description of the Nucleus, potentially AI-generated based on its name or purpose.

tags.description: An array of relevant tags associated with the Nucleus, potentially AI-generated.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the Nucleus was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the Nucleus was last updated.

BindCode.title: BindCode
BindCode.description: Represents a unique alphanumeric bind code generated by the system, potentially linked to a Nucleus.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BindCode entity.

code.description: The actual unique alphanumeric bind code, e.g., 'XXXX'.

description.description: An optional description or context for the bind code.

expirationDate.description: An optional date and time when the bind code expires.

status.description: The current status of the bind code (e.g., 'active', 'used', 'expired', 'revoked').

nucleusId.description: Reference to the Nucleus entity this bind code is associated with. (Relationship: Nucleus 1:N BindCode)

generatedAt.description: Timestamp when the bind code was generated.

BindHistoryEntry.title: BindHistoryEntry
BindHistoryEntry.description: Records a chronological log of all bind operations and their statuses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BindHistoryEntry entity.

bindCodeId.description: Reference to the BindCode entity involved in this operation. (Relationship: BindCode 1:N BindHistoryEntry)

nucleusId.description: Reference to the Nucleus entity associated with the bind code. (Relationship: Nucleus 1:N BindHistoryEntry via BindCode)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the bind operation occurred.

status.description: The status of the bind operation (e.g., 'pending', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'success').

details.description: Optional additional details or notes about the operation.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore data structure for BindNexus leverages a strictly hierarchical, user-owned model, implemented through path-based authorization and extensive denormalization. This design ensures robust security, high scalability, and simplifies Firestore security rules significantly.

1.  **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** This structure meticulously adheres to the principle of Authorization Independence by embedding all necessary authorization context directly within each document. For Nucleus entities, the document will include an `ownerId` field that matches the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, allowing rules to authorize access based solely on `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId`. For BindCode and BindHistoryEntry entities, the `ownerId` of the parent Nucleus, along with `nucleusId` and `bindCodeId` (for history), are denormalized into their respective documents. This completely eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to check parent ownership or related entity properties. Consequently, atomic operations (transactions and batched writes) remain performant and secure, and rules are simpler to write, understand, and debug.

2.  **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** The hierarchical path structure `users/{userId}/nuclei/{nucleusId}/bindCodes/{bindCodeId}/history/{historyEntryId}` intrinsically supports Query-Able Paths (QAPs). When a user performs a `list` operation on any of these collections (e.g., `/users/{request.auth.uid}/nuclei`), Firestore security rules can enforce `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;`. This ensures that the database itself will only return documents where the `userId` in the path matches the authenticated user's UID. The rules are not acting as filters after an initial broad query; instead, the query itself is constrained by the path, allowing Firestore to efficiently retrieve only the authorized data. This guarantees that `list` operations are secure, efficient, and predictable.
